$ xref dump

by Alexander Panasenko · xrefcode.com
On this page

Parallel modular pseudo-C dump grouped by recovered Rust source paths (<OUT>/crate/src/mod.c).

Groups stripped functions by embedded Rust panic file paths and writes modular .c files in parallel. Stdout and generated file preview are shown separately below.

Usage

xref dump [OPTIONS] --out <OUT>

Arguments and options

Options

--out <OUT>
Output directory for grouped .c module files.
--src <SRC>
Optional substring filter on source path or symbol name (e.g. src/loops.rs).
--fields
Rewrite raw pointer offsets as inferred ->f_<off> field hints.
--goto
Keep residual labels and gotos in every dumped function.

Examples

All examples were recorded on public binaries; see Provenance.

Dump --out out-loops --src src/loops.rs

Exports the 4 functions attributed to src/loops.rs into out-loops/src/loops.c.

Command
$ xref -b xref.stripped dump --out out-loops --src src/loops.rs
Output
dumped 4 functions into 1 files (12738 bytes) in out-loops (9.7ms)
stderr
xref: load 564.9µs, total 10.3ms

Reading the output

  • stdout is one summary line: how many functions went into how many files, the bytes written, the output directory and the time.
  • The files are <OUT>/<crate>/src/<module>.c, one per recovered Rust source path; each holds the pseudo-C of the functions whose panic locations point to that file.

Limits

  • Functions are grouped by the source paths of their panic locations; functions without any panic location are not exported by --src.

Provenance

Recorded with xref 0.5.0 (the remapped release build of commit b00d4a14, made by scripts/package-release.sh before the tag) on Linux x86-64, on xref.stripped = a stripped xref build (the binary of the home-page examples). Output is unchanged except that whitespace at the end of each line and empty lines at the end of the output are removed; long outputs are cut where marked.
